thesisQuality.note: Durable domestic steel demand and vertical integration are evidenced, but cyclical economics and substitute supply prevent a strong/exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Q2 adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow improved, while negative TTM earnings, leverage and cyclicality keep the assessment mixed.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Roughly $7.13B market cap and $14.78B EV against $19.20B TTM revenue provide plausible headroom, but negative TTM income and leverage prevent a favorable valuation conclusion.

catalystScore.note: Policy-backed Middletown modernization plus Q3 execution/debt-reduction potential are identifiable catalysts, with commissioning and return timing still uncertain.

governancePower.note: Long-tenured operating leadership and disclosed capital projects support adequate governance, but current evidence does not justify strong-band capital-allocation claims.

alignment2036.note: Domestic steel, electrical/automotive products and modernization capacity serve durable manufacturing and infrastructure needs, but are not irreplaceable across all futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Automotive, infrastructure/manufacturing, distributors/converters and steel-producer channels reuse integrated steel capabilities, though automotive concentration remains material.

bottleneckControl.note: Integrated iron ore/DRI/steelmaking/finishing creates meaningful domestic capacity control and qualification value, but alternative domestic and imported supply remain available.

scenarioRobustness.note: Multiple end markets and vertical integration provide resilience, offset by steel-cycle, automotive and trade-policy sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.note: Specialized sheet/electrical/stainless/plate products and qualification barriers support moderate replacement resistance, while imports, domestic peers and material substitution remain credible.

supplyChainResilience.note: Iron ore, pellets/DRI and downstream integration reduce upstream dependency, though energy, equipment, geographic and project dependencies remain.

pricingPower.note: Domestic scarcity and specialized products provide some pricing support, but commodity steel cycles and import/trade conditions constrain durable pass-through power.

risk.note: Material cyclicality, 29% automotive concentration, leverage, trade-policy exposure and project execution risk warrant elevated but not terminal risk.

confidence.note: Identity, filings, Q2 operating evidence and current independent valuation are source-addressed; future execution and operating-source independence remain limitations.

thesis: Cleveland-Cliffs combines domestic integrated steel capacity, specialized products and policy-backed modernization with durable infrastructure/manufacturing relevance, but the thesis remains constrained by cyclicality, automotive concentration and leverage.
keyRisk: A steel/automotive downturn or trade-policy reversal could compress utilization and pricing before project spending and debt reduction improve resilience.
nextCatalyst: Execution against post-Q2 free-cash-flow/debt-reduction expectations and progress on the Middletown modernization program.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore records the methodology-weighted component score; risk and confidence are separately source-addressed and remain subject to deterministic runtime gates/penalties.
